title: TAXKALSHI — Kalshi Tax Research Desk & Cost Calculator
description: Sourced research desk for how Kalshi earnings are taxed for a U.S. citizen who is a California resident paying tax in the ordinary way, outside withholding and penalty regimes. Because the character of event-contract income is open, a single-slider calculator computes the same $10,000 step through $200,000 under five candidate characters at once — ordinary, short-term capital, section 1256 (60/40), long-term capital, and wagering — and shows the difference; at $50,000 of modeled taxable income the federal figure is $5,752.00 / $5,752.00 / $2,234.50 / $82.50 / $5,752.00, while California is $1,534.89 in every scenario, and the README states the lower rows are not established for these contracts. The front page answers that Kalshi earnings are taxable, that event-contract character was not settled by any IRS ruling located by 2026-09-24, and that California taxes a resident’s taxable income at ordinary rates with no lower capital-gains rate. The site frames a decision engine as a panel of real verified public accountants licensed in California and the US that critique each other’s work, with the line-by-line record in data/findings.json, a critique table (engine.html), conflicts (flags.html) and a next-session reading list (method.html). Flagged: the CPA seats it frames are empty until verified, and its own rules forbid stating a 2026 California bracket until the Franchise Tax Board publishes the schedule.
